title: Big-O by counting
objective: See how the number of steps grows as the input grows, and name that growth: O(n), O(n²), O(log n).

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): growth of functions and O-notation

simplifies: Counting one "step" per loop pass hides that real steps differ in cost. Big-O keeps only how the count grows, which is what matters once n is large.

quiz.prompt: A loop inside a loop, each over n items, does about how many steps when n is 1,000?

options.explanation: Right. 1,000 outer passes × 1,000 inner passes = n² = 1,000,000.
That is two loops one after the other (n + n). Nested loops multiply: n × n.
That is a single loop. The inner loop runs fully for every outer pass.

quiz.prompt: Which grows slowest as n gets very large?

options.explanation: This grows fastest of the three: doubling n makes it 4 times as much.
Right. Doubling n adds just one step, so even a billion items take about 30 steps.
This grows in step with n. O(log n) grows much more slowly.
